paper.title: ZK-Tracer: A High-Performance Heterogeneous Accelerator for Zero-Knowledge VM Trace Generation
paper.summary: Zero-knowledge virtual machines (zkVMs) are a key technology for driving the large-scale adoption of zero-knowledge proofs (ZKP), but their performance bottlenecks severely limit their practicality. While current hardware acceleration research has exclusively focused on backend proving, we identify that the frontend execution and trace generation phase is rapidly emerging as the new system bottleneck. To address this challenge, we propose ZK-Tracer, the first hardware accelerator architecture specifically designed for the zkVM frontend. ZK-Tracer features a novel heterogeneous design comprising a Main Trace Unit and parallel Permutation Trace Units. It exposes a fine-grained interface to the host software through a lightweight instruction set extension, enabling efficient task offloading. Our ASIC implementation results demonstrate that ZK-Tracer achieves up to 1829x speedup in trace generation over a high-performance multi-core CPU. When integrated with existing backend proving accelerators, it delivers a remarkable 963x end-to-end performance improvement for the entire ZKP system.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the performance bottleneck in zero-knowledge virtual machines (zkVMs) during the frontend execution and trace generation phase.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Performance bottleneck in zkVM frontend execution and trace generation
analysis.executive_summary: This paper proposes ZK-Tracer, a hardware accelerator that significantly improves the performance of zero-knowledge virtual machines by addressing the frontend execution and trace generation bottleneck. This matters to the current AI landscape as it enables the large-scale adoption of zero-knowledge proofs, a crucial technology for secure and private AI computations. The proposed accelerator achieves remarkable speedups and end-to-end performance improvements.
